replies.content: Yes, it has been implemented in Poland, and our ID card was redesigned. This law is a blessing for me, as I work in compliance. Some EU countries have terrible ID cards, with close to zero security features. It's a nightmare for people like me. Greece, Italy (most people still have paper IDs), I'm looking at you guys. It's a real shame that they've been using crappy IDs like that for years.
Yes, its the 4.0 and it's ugly af, but the one before (3.0) was ugly too. I liked the 2.0
So basically they took the Spanish design and added a few things like the EU flag.
Finally an ID card that will fit with all your other cards !! The current one is WAY BIGGER you can't fit it in your wallet
Yes but I’m stuck with the old paper ID until 2028

Yes, we got them already. I helped at a vaccination center in the entry area and about half the people already got those. I was somewhat surprised at first because we last update ID cards less then ten years ago but this being a new European standard definitely explains it.
As far as I can tell, no. We don't even have a national ID cards and I can't find any Danish sources even mention this EU ID card thing.

Technically yes, but very little will change. The biggest changes are cosmetic - they changed the font on the front, the picture is on the other side, and the chip is on the back of the side instead of the front. Seems like this roll-out will be slow and steady since there are a bunch of valid ID cards out there. Source
